status: FIRST PASS — user-accepted for a first look, not a ratified render tier
source: web/results/july23/stack_set-01+02_desky_min_spcc.fit (799 frames, 13.2 Mpx, de-skied flats + per-frame subsky 1)

measured.note: corners came out BEST, not worst — attributed to the undistort stage keeping the PSF uniform across the field

measured.structure_selectivity: blank sky loses MORE than the gas region at every band (3-6px: -59.8% vs -52.9%; 12-24px: -45.4% vs -11.8%) — the denoiser spares real structure
measured.walking_noise: UNMASKED, not created: random pixel noise -58% while the horizontal band amplitude moved +1% (row/col anisotropy 2.40 -> 2.39). Pre-existing, BACKLOG item 11, acquisition-side fix is dithering (declined by user)

chain.params: low = 0.9273 x channel median, high = 1.16 x channel median, mid = 0.804 (common)
chain.why: black/white points PROPORTIONAL to each channel's own level so (sky - low) keeps the linear ratio BY CONSTRUCTION. A COMMON black point amplifies sub-1% linear colour differences into a ~10% render cast, because the sky sits only ~7% above black. Verified: sky-above-black ratios R/G 1.0022 B/G 1.0048 vs linear 1.0024 / 1.0047.
chain.why_superseded: The 'keeps the linear ratio BY CONSTRUCTION' claim was verified on (sky - low), the numerator, which the mtf then divides by (high - low). With the width ALSO scaling per channel the median factor cancels and the construction forces the sky to exactly neutral (verified numerically: 1.000036 / 1.000001) rather than preserving the linear ratio. The '~10% cast from a common black point' is a black-point DEPTH effect (-5.71% at f=0.02, -2.00% at f=0.073, -1.31% at f=0.139), compounded here by absolute points measured on the star-ful stack and applied to the starless+denoised layer. Current construction + numbers: scripts/stack/render_tier.sh and qa_work/render_set-01+02_desky_linked.json.

chain.why: -human preserves L*a*b* lightness so star colour survives compressing a 25000:1 range
screen — the exact inverse of starnet's unscreen split

residual_defects: COLOUR at the bright end: rendered gas R/G 0.990 B/G 0.928 vs linear truth 1.000 / 0.995. INHERENT to nonlinear stretching — any curve changes channel ratios because channels enter at different points and exit with different local slopes. Structurally worse here because the sky is only ~7% above black. The asinh variant (judge/set-01+02_desky_render_asinh.png) splits the error more evenly (R/G 0.960 B/G 0.951) but costs contrast (gas 69 -> 56) — neither is free.

HORIZONTAL BANDING: walking noise, ~2.4x more structure along rows than columns, near-horizontal because the drift axis is ~4 deg from horizontal. Rejection and cosmetic correction measure NULL against it; the fix is acquisition-side dithering.
STAR ELONGATION 1.196:1 — in-exposure trailing at 3 s, the unremovable floor. No processing touches it.

not_attempted_and_why.deconvolution: classical RL is a measured dead end on in-exposure trailing; BlurXTerminator not installed; GraXpert deconv is the immature path with an open object-mode artifact bug
not_attempted_and_why.star sharpening: a symmetric sharpener cannot de-trail an elongated PSF and may make it more obvious
